A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 36-page versions of the same GLGENN paper. The main text, Appendices A–I, equations, figures, and tables support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix I report original GLGENN experiments on regression, convex-hull volume estimation, and N-body prediction, including numerical errors and training times.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix I retain these original experimental results, including GLGENN performance and comparisons with other models.

M1.justification: The GLGENN architecture and weight-sharing procedure are unchanged. Section 4 retains the same embeddings, conjugation operations, linear layers, geometric-product layers, and normalization.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same O(5,0) regression, five- and seven-dimensional convex-hull tasks, and five-dimensional N-body prediction. Appendix I retains the same scenarios, including the larger point-cloud settings.

E2.justification: Tables 2 and 5 retain MLP, MLP+AUG, EMLP-O(5), EMLP-SO(5), and CGENN as regression comparators. The convex-hull, N-body, matched-parameter, and MLP-combination comparisons also retain identical comparator membership.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix I specify the same sample sizes, MSE metric, model configurations, training-step comparisons, batch sizes, and N-body simulation procedure. No evaluation protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same training/test-loss analyses, matched-parameter CGENN comparisons, and experiments combining geometric layers with MLPs. Figures 3–6 and Tables 9–11 provide unchanged evidence.

E5.justification: Repeated-run and uncertainty reporting are identical. Figure 2 retains 95% confidence intervals over five runs for regression and convex-hull estimation and three runs for N-body prediction.

E6.justification: All numerical results and plotted findings match, including Tables 2–3 and 5–12. For example, Table 12 retains GLGENN MSEs of 0.007, 0.0011, and 0.0009 and CGENN MSEs of 0.0136, 0.0015, and 0.0007.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions, theorems, derivations, and proofs in Sections 2–3 and Appendices B–H are unchanged. Minor equation positioning differences do not alter mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about generalized Lipschitz groups, pseudo-orthogonal equivariance, parameter efficiency, and competitive benchmark performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning parameter sharing, reduced overfitting, and interactions across grades are unchanged. Both versions retain the restriction of experiments to non-degenerate algebras and the qualification that parameter-efficiency differences emerge only above dimension three.

D1.justification: The implementation descriptions, parameter counts, batch-size information, training-time reporting, and code-access information remain identical, including Appendix I. No reproducibility details are added or removed.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including the relationship to CGENN and other geometric-algebra approaches. The reference list contains no added or removed works.

P1.justification: The arXiv margin header changes from v1, 11 Jun 2025 to v2, 3 Dec 2025. The paper's prose, terminology, section order, and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: There are slight typesetting shifts, notably the horizontal placement of Equation (13). Figures 1–6 and Tables 1–12 retain their content, captions, structure, and placement.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, empirical evidence, proofs, interpretations, and reproducibility information are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. The updated version stamp and cosmetic typesetting differences produce no meaningful overall quality gain or loss.
